kind.description: concept teaches, misconception names the wrong turn most people take.

line.description: One spoken line. What this character says on this beat. No quotation marks, no speaker name.

speaker_body.description: Who is speaking. Alternate between them; a stretch of the same speaker reads as a monologue. Options: mei = Mei, hime cut, brown hair, navy seifuku, round glasses. She explains and is usually right.; hana = Hana, twin tails, dark hair, white seifuku. She asks, guesses, and is often wrong first.

speaker_face.description: The speaker's expression. Options: normal = level and attentive. The default for a plain explanation.; smile = a small closed smile, warm and unhurried.; pleased = eyes closed, gently pleased. Use when something has just landed.; laugh = eyes closed, open-mouthed, delighted.; delighted = bright and open-mouthed, genuinely excited by the idea.; shocked = wide eyes, mouth open. Use when a result is genuinely surprising.; sad = downcast brows, quiet. Use when an approach did not work.; angry = brows down, mouth open. Rare, and only for a firm correction.; smug = one brow up, a small knowing smile. Use when the answer was obvious in hindsight.; annoyed = flat eyes, unimpressed. Use for a mistake that keeps coming back.; sleepy = heavy lids. Use sparingly, for a long or dry stretch.

background.description: Where the scene takes place. Chosen once for the module. Options: classroom-day = an empty classroom in daylight, desks in rows. The default setting.; library = a wide school library with tall windows. For research, reading, quiet work.; corridor-morning = a school corridor in morning light. For short scenes and asides.; school-gate = the school entrance, trees and open sky. For beginnings and endings.; basketball-court = an indoor court. For anything physical, competitive, or about movement.

ask_line.description: The closing line, spoken to the student after the last beat. Land what was just worked out, then ask where they want to go next. It must end in a question.
